experiment_name: ASU-value-v1 as evaluation opponent only (short single-seed benchmark)
exact_commands: PYTHONHASHSEED=0 python scripts/run_baseline_match.py --focus asu-value-v1 --opponents fixed-a fixed-b fixed-c --seed 20000 --output docs/baseline_runs/asu_eval_probe_seed20000.json

algorithm_config.asu_role: evaluation opponent only - no ASU output, action, value, or rollout data was collected, imitated, distilled, or used as a training label

metrics.not_a_strength_claim: single seed, n=4, extremely wide Wilson interval

result: ASU-value-v1 runs cleanly as a fixed evaluation opponent: 0 illegal actions, 0 crashes, 0 fallbacks from ASU itself (all 36 fallbacks in the block came from fixed-a/b/c). Its cost (~531.7s/game blended average) is roughly 1,000x slower per decision than fixed/DDQN agents, due to its 5-turn dice-enumeration + 5-lap landing-distribution heuristic evaluated per legal action per decision. This cost is the real constraint on ever using it as a monopoly_bench collect-asu teacher signal at scale - not investigated as training, since ASU may only be an evaluation opponent per CLAUDE.md.
notes: Only one seed was run given the measured cost; the same 10000-10009 range used for the DDQN evaluations would extrapolate to roughly 15-20 CPU-hours at this rate. peak_rss_gib is null (not separately measured for this run).
